---
title: "3.2 Switches and Floating Inputs"
description: "Explain why an open switch needs a pull resistor to establish a defined GPIO state."
sidebar: tej
toc: true
execute: {enabled: false}
---

A closed switch can connect an input to a voltage rail. An open switch disconnects that path. Without another connection, a high-impedance input floats and can respond to leakage, nearby signals, static charge, or a hand near the wire.

![An unconnected GPIO input is marked incorrect because no circuit establishes a defined voltage.](/assets/tej/Floating_Input.svg){fig-alt="An unconnected wire enters a GPIO input. A red X marks the floating wire as incorrect." width=90%}

| Switch position | Electrical connection | Pin voltage | Logical state |
|:--|:--|:--|:--:|
| closed to ground | ground | near $0\ \mathrm{V}$ | 0 |
| closed to supply | $V_{CC}$ | near $V_{CC}$ | 1 |
| open without a pull | none | undefined | invalid |

Arduino's official digital-pin documentation notes that an input with nothing connected can report apparently random state changes. [Read the Arduino digital-pin reference](https://docs.arduino.cc/learn/microcontrollers/digital-pins/).

## Evidence check

Predict the pin state before simulation. If a simulator displays a stable 0 or 1 for a floating input, record that as a simulator limitation rather than proof of a valid physical design.
